A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MIMETIC2 imitation-threshold study despite the changed title. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching material across substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original imitation thresholds, human-subject evaluations, face-encoder comparisons, and analyses of assumptions and outliers.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds LDM evaluations, controlled finetuning experiments, classifier metrics, and resampling-based threshold estimates.

M1.justification: The concept filtering/counting, domain-specific similarity scoring, and first-PELT-change procedure remain unchanged. Comparing generated images with the ten most similar training images, now explicit in the main text, already appeared in v1 Appendices E.2 and F.2. The finetuning experiments validate MIMETIC2 rather than modify it.

E1.justification: Coverage expands within the existing human-face and art-style domains through LAION-400M and a focused collection of newly popular people reported absent from pretraining, used for finetuning validation. The four main sets of 400 concepts remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v2 adds a finetuning-based reference comparison: approximately 250 images are required in the intervention experiment versus MIMETIC2's 234-image SD1.4 estimate (Appendices C.2 and H). The eight face-encoder comparators remain unchanged. LDM is an additional model being measured, not a competing threshold-estimation method.

E3.justification: v2 replaces the cross-set accuracy proxy with controlled SD1.4 finetuning validation using 50–800 target images, mixtures totaling 10,000 images, one epoch, and learning rate 5e-5. It also adds a fixed-400-image subset experiment and classifier accuracy, precision, and recall reporting. The original five-prompt, 200-images-per-prompt generation protocol remains unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices C.2–C.3 add interventions testing the absence-of-confounders and equal-image-contribution assumptions, which v1 did not empirically test. v2 also adds distributional evidence for invariance and quantitative classifier diagnostics. Existing encoder ablations and most outlier analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v1 reports prompt variability but no resampled uncertainty for its threshold estimates. v2 adds 1,000 concept-subset resamples, termed a permutation test, and reports threshold means and standard errors. Its new image-subset experiment repeats finetuning 20 times and reports means, standard deviations, and distributions.

E6.justification: Table 3 replaces point estimates with resampled summaries: SD1.1 celebrities change from 364 to 399 ± 3 and classical styles from 112 to 304 ± 2. These are changed statistical summaries, not performance gains. v2 adds LDM, finetuning, and classifier results, while removing extrapolated missed-image counts from v1 Table 5. Older thresholds remain in appendix tables and some captions, including captions that disagree with updated plots.

T1.justification: The formal threshold definition, counterfactual setup, and three underlying assumptions are retained. The added invariance equation restates v1's existing prose. New empirical assumption checks do not introduce a theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The central problem and MIMETIC2 contribution remain intact. The headline empirical scope expands from three models and two pretraining datasets to four models and three datasets, and the stated threshold range changes from 200–600 to 200–700. v2 adds a quantified validation claim and removes v1's explicit conclusion that concepts appearing fewer than 200 times cannot be imitated.

C2.justification: v2 interprets its finetuning studies as validating all three assumptions and approximating ground-truth thresholds; v1 tested only invariance and explicitly questioned equal image contributions. New Appendix B specifies dependence on sampled concepts, detector quality, and change-point selection. v2 also hypothesizes that LDM's higher thresholds reflect its smaller pretraining corpus.

D1.justification: v2 documents the new finetuning experiments' concept sources, image mixtures, learning rate, epoch count, and imitation-score criterion. These are details of added experiments rather than evidence that retained experiments changed settings. Existing reference-image collection, filtering thresholds, hardware, timing, and repository information are largely retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including He et al. (2024), Schuhmann et al. (2021), and Yao et al. (2025). It removes the explicit Dreambooth/Imagic comparison and associated citations. The main positioning around concept frequency, imitation, and observational estimation, including Appendix A, remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The title changes, FIT terminology is dropped, and substantial passages in the introduction, formulation, methodology, results, and limitations are rewritten. Methodology now precedes experimental setup. The appendices are reorganized with dedicated applicability and validation sections, beyond simply inserting additional results.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different publication layout and substantially resizes and relocates existing displays. It adds distribution plots, finetuning and classifier tables, and LDM plots; Table 3 gains uncertainty reporting and an LDM row. The caption-occurrence table loses its extrapolated-count column, and several updated plots retain outdated captions.

improvement.justification: The controlled finetuning checks, threshold resampling, and explicit applicability conditions provide useful support beyond v1's cross-set accuracy argument. The gain is limited by overinterpreting finetuning as the training-from-scratch counterfactual and by reporting inconsistencies: Figure 29 plots a threshold of 304 but captions it as 112, while Appendix C's ±0.2% variability claim does not match Table 6's standard deviations of 0.02–0.03.
